claims.headline: Reported Central London availability down 20% year on year
claims.text: Semafor reported on 9 October 2026 that Canary Wharf Group's latest earnings showed Central London availability fell 20% year on year while Docklands supply stayed broadly steady. This is attributed secondary reporting of a landlord's earnings, not a normalized availability series.

claims.headline: Canary Wharf Group reports record rents and 92%+ occupancy
claims.text: Semafor reported on 9 October 2026 that Canary Wharf Group is reporting the highest rental rates in its history, with office occupancy above 92% and visitor numbers on track to exceed last year's record of 76 million. Publisher-reported levels; no averaging window or reference period is stated.

claims.headline: Reported occupier commitments across London offices
claims.text: Semafor reported on 9 October 2026 that Visa recently leased 300,000 sq ft, Barclays bought its headquarters for £750 million, Citi is investing over $1 billion in its European HQ, and JPMorgan has proposed a £3 billion, 265-metre tower subject to approval. Deal dates and areas are not established.

claims.headline: Landlord reports majority of occupiers expanding
claims.text: Canary Wharf Group's chief executive said roughly 60% of its office occupiers grew their footprint over the last 18 months, 20% were stable and 20% shrank. This is a single landlord's portfolio experience, not a London-wide demand measure.

claims.headline: Tenants said to prioritise quality space for talent
claims.text: Canary Wharf's chief executive said tenants hold differing return-to-office policies but increasingly agree they need the best space to compete for talent. Attributed occupier-preference commentary, not measured London attendance or floor-space demand.

claims.headline: Canary Wharf refurbishment marketed to defence and AI occupiers
claims.text: Reuters-sourced reporting dated 5 October 2026 said developer LS Estates is sounding out defence and AI companies for a refurbished nine-floor Canary Wharf office formerly occupied by Credit Suisse support staff. Marketing interest, not a signed lease or completed letting.

claims.headline: Canary Wharf lab-led refit sees weaker life-science interest
claims.text: Reporting dated 5 October 2026 said the £100 million-plus refit of 17 Columbus Courtyard in Canary Wharf, backed by GIC and Oaktree, had earmarked up to 60% of space for laboratories but life-sciences interest was lower than expected in the short term. Refurbishment status, not completed supply.

claims.headline: Knight Frank: development lagging occupier demand
claims.text: Knight Frank commentary published 7 October 2026 said London office development activity is not keeping pace with occupier demand for the type of space now required, driven partly by viability pressures and macroeconomic caution. Attributed interpretation with no measurement period.

claims.headline: Central London Q2 2026 take-up 2.4 million sq ft
claims.text: Savills reported Central London take-up of 2.4 million sq ft across 192 transactions in Q2 2026 (April to June). This is a quarterly flow, not a weekly measurement.

claims.headline: Central London take-up up 0.2 million sq ft quarter on quarter
claims.text: Savills Central London take-up rose from 2.2 million sq ft in Q1 2026 to 2.4 million sq ft in Q2 2026, a 0.2 million sq ft increase (about 9.1%). Quarterly comparison, not week over week.

claims.headline: Central London vacancy 7.2% at end-Q2 2026
claims.text: Savills reported the Central London vacancy rate declined 20 basis points to 7.2% at end-Q2 2026, from 7.4% at end-Q1 2026. Vacancy is distinct from availability.

claims.headline: City vacancy unchanged at 7.0%
claims.text: Savills reported the City vacancy rate remained unchanged at 7.0% at end-Q2 2026. A level with no direction, and not an availability measure.

claims.headline: Central London reported supply down 0.4 million sq ft
claims.text: Savills reported Central London reported supply fell from 19.1 million sq ft at end-Q1 2026 to 18.7 million sq ft at end-Q2 2026, a 0.4 million sq ft decline (about 2.1%). Reported supply is not a vacancy rate.

claims.headline: West End H1 2026 average prime rent £175.10 per sq ft
claims.text: Savills reported West End average prime rent of £175.10 per sq ft for H1 2026 (January to June), up 2.3% on H1 2025. Average prime rent from leasing transactions, not asking rent.

claims.headline: City year-to-date achieved prime rent £135 per sq ft
claims.text: Savills reported the average achieved City prime rent for the year to date at £135 per sq ft as of 30 June 2026, a January-to-May cumulative average. It is not comparable with the H1 West End average.

claims.headline: H1 2026 Grade A rents: City £76.21, West End £106.17
claims.text: Savills reported City average Grade A rent of £76.21 per sq ft for H1 2026, up 7% on H1 2025, and West End average Grade A rent of £106.17 per sq ft at end-H1 2026. Grade A averaging windows are unspecified.

claims.headline: Savills forecasts 22 million sq ft completions by 2029
claims.text: Savills forecasts Central London development completions reaching 22 million sq ft by end-2029 across 148 schemes, with 28% of that future supply not yet commenced and therefore vulnerable to delay or withdrawal. Source forecast, not current availability.

claims.headline: H1 2026 development starts 1.5 million sq ft
claims.text: Savills reported Central London development starts fell sharply in H1 2026 to just 1.5 million sq ft, with only one new-build scheme breaking ground (Delta at Paddington, 234,000 sq ft) and the remaining 14 starts being refurbishments. Starts are not future pipeline area.

claims.headline: 1 Appold Street pre-let 268,000 sq ft at £104 per sq ft
claims.text: Savills reported the largest pre-let and transaction to complete was Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer's acquisition of 1 Appold Street, EC2 (268,000 sq ft) at £104 per sq ft for a 21-year term, published 1 May 2026. Historical pre-let context.

claims.headline: Grade A was 78% of Q1 2026 Central London take-up
claims.text: BNP Paribas Real Estate reported Grade A space accounted for 78.0% of all Central London take-up in Q1 2026. A share of take-up, not of stock, and not evidence of a widening quality premium.

claims.headline: BREEAM-rated buildings show 39-49% rent premium
claims.text: Savills reported that in H1 2026 average rents in BREEAM 'Excellent' or 'Outstanding' buildings were 49% higher than non-rated buildings in the West End and 39% higher in the City. A static premium, not a widening gap or causal amenity effect.

claims.headline: Deutsche Bank to take Canary Wharf space from 2028
claims.text: Deutsche Bank announced it will take space at YY London, Canary Wharf, from early 2028, in a building described as fully electric and targeting net-zero-in-operation. Announced future plan, not observed occupation or verified net-zero achievement.

claims.headline: London resident employment 73.9% in May-July 2026
claims.text: ONS reported London residents' employment rate of 73.9%, unemployment rate of 6.8% and inactivity rate of 20.5% for May to July 2026. Residence-based LFS estimates, not London workplace or office employment.

claims.headline: ONS labour estimates are residence-based
claims.text: ONS stated LFS, APS and RTI estimates are based on the region where someone lives rather than where they work, so London resident labour figures are not London workplace jobs or office attendance.

claims.headline: London professional job vacancies down 11% year on year
claims.text: Morgan McKinley's London Employment Monitor reported professional job vacancies in London fell to 4,368 in Q3 2026, down 6% quarter on quarter and 11% year on year, with monthly vacancies falling from 1,719 in July to 1,200 in September. Professional recruitment vacancies, not office vacancy.

claims.headline: Bank Rate held at 3.75% on 16 September 2026
claims.text: The Bank of England's MPC voted 6-3 on 16 September 2026 to maintain Bank Rate at 3.75%. A UK-wide policy rate, not a London office financing cost.

claims.headline: UK CPI inflation 3.1% in August 2026
claims.text: The Bank of England reported UK CPI inflation increased to 3.1% in August 2026. Observed UK inflation, not a London-specific rate or a rent forecast.

GLA Economics estimates suggest a modest strengthening of London economic growth, with real GVA expected to have risen 1.1% in 2024 and 1.9% in 2025. GLA estimates, not observed official outturn, and London-wide context rather than office-market measurement.
claims.headline: GLA estimates modest London GVA strengthening
GLA attributes London worklessness to weaker labour demand
claims.text: GLA commentary attributed recent involuntary worklessness in London mainly to weaker labour-market demand. Attributed interpretation; the exact survey window is unspecified and it is not an office-employment measure.

claims.headline: 28% of GB working adults hybrid in early 2025
claims.text: ONS reported 28% of working adults in Great Britain were hybrid workers between 8 January and 30 March 2025. Great Britain survey context, not London office attendance, and now stale.

claims.headline: City Fringe vacancy 8.2% at end-Q4 2025
claims.text: Savills reported City Fringe vacancy of 8.2% at end-Q4 2025, down from 8.3% at end-Q3 2025. City Fringe is not Midtown, and Midtown itself remains unmeasured.

claims.headline: Hammersmith 26% and VNEB 18% vacancy in Q4 2025
claims.text: Savills reported Q4 2025 vacancy of 26% in Hammersmith and 18% in VNEB, West End Fringe sub-markets. Selected wider-London districts, not representative of all wider London.

claims.headline: Turing Building at Stratford Cross 350,000 sq ft
claims.text: Lendlease reported the Turing Building at Stratford Cross provides 350,000 sq ft of Grade A office space, the first building delivered in its joint venture with CPP Investments. Building area, not take-up or current availability; completion date not established.

claims.headline: Stratford Cross final phase plans submitted
claims.text: Lendlease reported plans submitted to the London Borough of Newham for the final phase of Stratford Cross, proposing about 2,000 homes plus a public park and retail space. A submitted residential-led proposal, not consented or completed office supply.

claims.headline: Lambeth approves London Fire Brigade HQ refurbishment
claims.text: The London Fire Brigade received planning permission from Lambeth Council to return to its historic Albert Embankment headquarters, with the site to be refurbished to provide a fire station, office space and community spaces. Announced permission and plan, not completed refurbishment.

claims.headline: Unstarted pipeline is the key supply swing factor
claims.text: If the 28% of Savills' forecast Central London pipeline that has not yet started construction is delayed or withdrawn, landlords in core submarkets would face less competing new supply, but also fewer options for occupiers seeking large modern floorplates. Premise is a source forecast, not observed delivery.

claims.headline: Central London supply-demand balance broadly stable
claims.text: With City vacancy flat at 7.0% and Central London vacancy easing to 7.2% at end-Q2 2026, the balance of evidence points to a broadly stable rather than tightening Central London market. Quarterly data only; no weekly measurement exists.

claims.headline: Watch for corroboration of availability decline
claims.text: Watch whether the reported 20% year-on-year fall in Central London availability is corroborated by a reviewed availability series with a stated reference period, and whether Docklands supply stays broadly steady.

claims.headline: Watch Canary Wharf refurbishment lettings
claims.text: Watch whether the 17 Columbus Courtyard refit converts to signed lettings, and whether LS Estates secures defence or AI occupiers for the former Credit Suisse space, as evidence of Canary Wharf demand diversification.

claims.headline: Watch approval and completion of reported commitments
claims.text: Watch whether JPMorgan's proposed 265-metre tower receives approval and whether the reported Visa, Barclays and Citi commitments convert to dated completions, since none currently establish signed terms or occupation dates.

evidence.excerpt: The £100 million-plus ($130 million-plus) refit of 17 Columbus Courtyard — backed by Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC and Oaktree — was originally targeted at life sciences firms with up to 60 per cent of the space ​earmarked for laboratories, but Swetman said ​interest from that sector had been ⁠lower than expected in the short term.

Located at Stratford Cross, the Turing Building includes 350,000 square feet of sustainable Grade A office space and was designed by architects Arney Fender Katsalidis. It’s the first building to be delivered as part of Lendlease’s joint venture with Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPP Investments) at Stratford Cross on the edge of the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park.

evidence.excerpt: Khan can also boast a string of new commitments from high-profile global tenants. Visa recently leased 300,000 square feet of office space, Barclays just bought its headquarters for £750 million, and Citi is investing more than $1 billion in its European HQ. Capping them all is JPMorgan’s proposal to erect a £3 billion, 265-meter tower that will be London’s largest office building if its plans are approved.

Overall, based on our analysis of the development pipeline (with a view on schemes with a realistic prospect of delivery), development completions are expected to reach 22 million sq ft by the end of 2029, with 148 schemes scheduled for completion over this period. However, 28% of this future supply has yet to commence construction and therefore remains vulnerable to further delays or potential withdrawal as viability pressures persist.
